subject: gunblade
pitch:
Category: Weapon.
Subject: gunblade.
Style: Final Fantasy.

spec.name: Lionheart Gunblade
spec.description: A Final Fantasy VIII-style gunblade standing upright on its pommel: a long single-edged silver blade with a revolver mechanism in the hilt, gold filigree, glowing crystals and a lion pendant on a chain.
spec.layout: Static prop, no joints, standing upright on its flat round pommel base (y=0) with the blade pointing up; the tip is at y=1.5. From bottom to top: pommel disc and wrapped grip (y 0-0.40), revolver mechanism (0.40-0.66), winged crossguard (0.66-0.80), blade (0.80-1.50). The single-edged blade is a thin slab in the YZ plane, about 0.03 thick in x. Its sharp edge faces -Z, and its thick spine faces +Z toward the front. The trigger, trigger guard and a protruding hammer all face +Z. The revolver cylinder sits just below the crossguard with its axis along X, and its six chambers show on both x sides. The lion pendant hangs from a ring at the pommel's +X side on a short chain and rests on the floor beside the base, leaning slightly. Silhouette: a slim, elegant, slightly ornate Final Fantasy blade. A tall, narrow blade is contrasted by a chunky gun block and flared gold wing-shaped guard tips (tips curve upward and slightly back). Every part follows one three-layer colour rule: dark ink outline or recess, main colour, bright highlight line. Metal is cool silver-blue and trim is warm gold. Glowing crystal accents in cyan (blade runes, guard gem) and ruby (pommel gem) use the glow kit. The lion motif repeats on the guard centre, the cylinder side plates, the pommel cap and the pendant. Blocky faceted primitives only; detail comes from small seated parts.

parts.builds: The blade from y=0.80 to the tip at y=1.50, built as stacked thin extrudes sharing the same x/y axes. Main plate: steelLight, an outline running from a ricasso (z -0.07..0.05 at y 0.80) to a clipped, angled point at the tip (tip at z 0.02). The back edge has a long bevel strip in edgeBright running the full edge length, and a thin ink line between the bevel and the plate. The spine (+Z side) is a thicker steelMid strip (0.05 thick) with a row of small ink notches. The upper third of the spine carries the revolver-style barrel ridge: a slim gunmetal bar with a dark muzzle slit at the tip's underside. On both x faces there is a long recessed fuller groove in fullerBlue with an edgeBright highlight line above it, tapering toward the tip. 4-5 tiny rune glyphs (crystalCyan, glowing) are inset along the fuller. A lion engraving (steelDark) sits near the ricasso. Two or three gold rivets. A jagged cut-out of 3 notches near the tip on the edge side (Squall-style), outlined in ink. The tang is a steelDark block hidden down into the guard (y 0.76-0.80). Very thin faceted bevel pieces, nothing round.
parts.attaches: The base sits on the guard at bladeBase (y=0.80), centred at z=-0.015. The tang drops into the guard's blade slot. Nothing else touches the blade.

parts.builds: The ornate winged crossguard from y=0.66 to 0.80. A central gold block (goldDark underside, goldLight top highlight) with an ink-outlined diamond window holding a glowing crystalCyan gem on both x faces. Wing-shaped extruded arms sweep out to x=±0.20 in gold, curving upward and slightly back (-Z) at the tips. Each arm is built as layered feathers (3 stacked blades, goldDark, gold, goldLight tips) with a steelMid inner plate and tiny ink slits. A lion head emblem (lionSilver face, gold mane spikes, ink eyes) is on the +Z front of the central block. Beneath the guard is a thin steelMid collar plate and small rivets (goldLight). A ricasso collar (steelDark ring) surrounds the blade slot on top. Mirrored left and right with identical geometry.
parts.attaches: The underside meets the gun mechanism's top plate at y=0.66, aligned with cylinderCenter's x=0 and z about -0.01. Its top is at the bladeBase mount (y=0.80), where the blade's tang enters.

parts.builds: The revolver block from y=0.40 to 0.66. A gunmetal frame of two side plates (x=±0.055) joined by a top and a back strap, with gunmetalLight bevel edges and ink seams. The revolver cylinder (axis along X, radius about 0.055, 6 flutes, steelMid body with steelDark flutes) sits at cylinderCenter. Six round chamber holes (ink) with brassShell cartridge rims show on each x end and ring a gold centre pin. The side plates carry a gold lion-head medallion and engraved line trim in goldDark. At the front (+Z): the barrel stub under the blade spine (gunmetal, dark ink muzzle), a protruding hammer on hammerPivot (gunmetalLight with ink-grooved spur), and a steelMid trigger that pivots at triggerPivot, curving forward inside a slim gold trigger guard loop (swept tube) reaching z=0.22 and down to y=0.41. A small ruby crystal indicator (glowing) sits on the frame top. Small gold screws and a glowing crystalDeep slit in the frame's front face.
parts.attaches: The bottom plate sits on the grip's top cap at gripTop (y=0.40). The top plate meets the guard's underside at y=0.66. The grip's top tang runs up into the frame's back strap at z=0.

parts.builds: The handle from y=0 to 0.40, standing on the floor. A flat round pommel base (steelDark disc, radius about 0.065, flat bottom at y=0, gold rim ring, goldLight bevel) rises into a faceted pommel cap (steelMid, 8 sides) with a lion-head emblem (gold, ink eyes) on each x face and a glowing ruby gem at the front (+Z). The grip itself is a slim 8-sided column wrapped in leather (leather) with diagonal wrap bands in leatherRed as small slanted strips, spaced evenly. Gold collar rings at the top (y 0.38-0.40) and bottom (y 0.14-0.16), with ink groove lines. The top cap is a flat steelDark plate for the mechanism to sit on, with a small gold ring. A gold chain ring (torus, ink hole) is attached to the +X side of the pommel at chainRing, with a small gold pin.
parts.attaches: The base is on the floor at pommelBase (y=0). The top meets the gun mechanism at gripTop (y=0.40). The chain ring at chainRing is where the charm's chain attaches.

parts.builds: The lion pendant on a chain. A chain of about 10-12 small steel links (chainSteel, small alternating tori or rods) hangs in a curve from chainRing (0.075,0.09,-0.02), out to x about 0.17, and down to the pendant. The pendant is a round lionSilver medallion (radius about 0.04, ink outline ring, goldLight rim) with a lion-head relief in steelMid: ink eyes, a small ruby nose, a cream-silver muzzle, ink mouth line. A mane of 12-14 gold spikes (alternating gold and goldDark) rings the medallion, and a small gold bail loop at the top joins the chain. Two small feather charms (white-silver lionSilver and steelDark shade, 3 blades each) hang off the lower right side. The pendant is propped on the floor with its lowest mane spike at y about 0, tilted slightly (about 10 degrees) toward +Z. Everything is faceted and low-poly.
parts.attaches: The chain starts at the grip part's chainRing mount (0.075, 0.09, -0.02). The pendant rests on the floor next to the pommel base without touching it (x >= 0.12).

calls.reasoning:
I'm thinking through a gunblade design, Final Fantasy style like Squall's weapon—likely a static model without joints since it's a prop, needing to be oriented so it rests properly on the floor, perhaps standing vertically with the blade tip touching ground.

I'm deciding whether the blade points up or down, settling on a planted sword look with the tip sunk slightly into the floor, hilt up, trigger mechanism facing forward, blade edge oriented to one side as a single-edged revolver-style weapon.

Now I'm thinking it could rest pommel-down on the floor with the blade pointing up for a heroic display, about 1.4-1.5m tall, with Final Fantasy-style ornate details — silver blade, blue gradient, gold trim, lion emblem with glowing crystals and a lanyard chain. I'm roughing out dimensions: roughly 0.34m wide, 1.5m tall, 0.5m deep, accounting for the trigger guard, gun body, blade spine, and deciding where the pendant chain should hang so it doesn't complicate the floor placement.

I'm sorting out the vertical layout — pommel from 0 to 0.12m, grip 0.12-0.42, gun/hilt section 0.42-0.62, and blade spanning 0.62-1.5m — with a lion pendant charm hanging from the pommel ring, looping outward and resting on the floor as its own separate part. I'm settling on five main parts total, starting with the blade component.

Thinking through the blade's cross-section like Squall's Revolver gunblade: the spine faces +Z with the trigger mechanism on that side, cutting edge faces -Z, extruded in X with 0.03 thickness, blade profile running from z=-0.07 (edge) to z=+0.05 (spine), tapering to a clipped tip at y=1.5, with a fuller groove, ricasso, and spine notches.

Now I'm working out the hilt/gunbody section between y 0.40–0.68: a revolver cylinder with six visible chambers, hammer, trigger and guard, frame plates with gold trim, and an ejection slit, positioning the cylinder along the X-axis with radius 0.055 near y=0.58 where the blade's spine passes through.

Mapping out mount points — blade base, guard center, cylinder center, grip top/bottom, pommel, trigger pivot, and a chain anchor for a charm — then moving to the crossguard/wings design with a lion-head emblem and gold ornament spanning roughly y 0.62–0.78.

I'm splitting the sword into five parts with a budget: blade, guard, gun mechanism (cylinder, hammer, trigger, trigger guard, frame), grip+pommel with rings and gem, and the charm (chain, lion pendant, tassel), totaling 840 units. Now I'm positioning the gun body box and figuring out how the trigger guard loop hangs below the front.

Next I'm working out overall bounding dimensions—widening the guard wings and accounting for the charm's extension so the total size covers roughly x:0.44, y:1.5, z:0.36, with the blade tip capping at y=1.5 and the pommel base flat at y=0. I'm deciding to skip rigging joints since this isn't a creature, keeping the joints array empty for simplicity, then moving on to think about the color palette.

Rounding out the palette with ruby and brass tones, then planning where to use the glow kit for cyan crystals and ruby accents against dark gunmetal chambers. I'm starting to lay out the grip geometry as a floor-anchored box shape, coordinating how each part's bounding box will share faces with neighbors.

Mapping out the rest of the body: pommel disc with wrap and gem rings, the gun frame and cylinder, the guard overlapping slightly with the gun's top, and the blade emerging from the guard with a tang running through it, defining width from edge to spine.

I'm placing the charm and chain near the ring, sizing the lion pendant with mane spikes and checking that total extents stay within bounds given the guard width of 0.4.

I'll place the pendant disc as a ring shape around center (0.17, 0.065, 0), with the lion mane tapering down toward the floor, letting the chain drape loosely with the pendant resting leaning against the ground. Now I'm writing out the final spec with mount points and style details—Final Fantasy inspired silver blade with cyan crystal, gold filigree, lion motif, and wing accents—leaving joints empty as I compose the JSON.
